story: On a breezy, clear Friday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is out on Magnolia Loop stretching his legs while his golf cart kit waits in the garage for Architectural Review's sign-off, and he chats with Hal about the sketches heading to committee. Donna, looking determined, walks over to join them on the street, while Rosa bakes a big batch of treats in her kitchen for tomorrow's trick-or-treaters and parade crowd. Everyone's buzzing about Halloween on the Loop, with trick-or-treating from 5 to 7, the golf cart parade at 6, and the costume contest at the bandstand at 7.
events: Town news: Reminder on the bulletin board: Halloween on the Loop is tomorrow. Trick-or-treating 5 to 7 PM, the golf cart parade at 6, and the costume contest at the Town Square bandstand at 7.
Donna headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Bake a big batch of treats for Saturday's trick-or-treaters and parade crowd

gary.thought_process: I just got to Magnolia Loop, and Hal is the only one around. He asked about my cart last time and I told him straight that the application is filed but not approved, so nothing has changed there. The kit is packed and I'm doing this the honest way, so I'm not going to rush ahead of Architectural Review. Still, it's Halloween weekend, and Hal is a neighbor I like talking to. A friendly hello and a mention of the parade plans fits my need to feel useful, and I can offer to lend a hand with whatever he's got going.

parameters.content: Morning, Hal. Kit's all packed and ready for when Architectural Review signs off, so I'm just out stretching my legs. You got anything around the house you need a hand with before the parade tomorrow?

donna.thought_process: I've already checked the calendar and packed the bag. Nobody is in line-of-sight, and Gary is nowhere to be found since yesterday afternoon. Court time is limited to 2 hours per party under L-05, so I need to get to the courts before the Halloween weekend crowd and catch Gary there or on the way. Time to head out onto Magnolia Loop, bag in hand, and track down my reluctant partner.

parameters.content: Heading out to Magnolia Loop with my pickleball bag to find Gary and get those third-shot drops going.

hal.thought_process: Gary just walked up. My reflections say he's been moving his work into the garage and waiting on the committee, and I've been logging the street like a sentry. I'd rather talk with the man than watch him. I read the Halloween flyer last tick, so no need to read the board again. Cart parade is tonight's talk anyway. A straight, neighborly word about the cart and the committee is better than a report.

parameters.content: Morning, Gary. Heard you moved the cart work into the garage. Appreciate that. Bring those sketches to the committee and I'll hold my fire till they rule.

rosa.thought_process: I'm at home Friday morning with the parade tomorrow. I already checked my shift schedule and started on baking treats last tick, so the next step is to actually bake the batch for trick-or-treaters and the parade crowd. No one's around to talk to, so the kitchen is the productive move.

parameters.content: Bake a big batch of treats for Saturday's trick-or-treaters and parade crowd

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
